_doc: Rogueloot item bases. Every row is hand-specified (kind, drop level, grid, reqs, look); the damage and armour NUMBERS come from the two ladders below so the whole game scales from one place. Weapon dps ladder: refDps(L) = 4 + 1.5*L + 0.02*L*L for a ONE-HANDED weapon at drop level L; a kind multiplies it (`kinds[kind].dps`: two-handers 1.35, bows 1.2, wands 0.6 + spell power). damage.min/max = refDps*dpsMult/speed * [0.75, 1.25]. speed = attacks per second. Monster health should be tuned so a same-level normal monster dies to ~6-10 weapon hits. Armour ladder: damage reduction = armour / (armour + K) with K = 10*attackerLevel + 50 (that is ruling 41, armour diminishing against attacker level). A full plate set at level L sums to 1.5*K(L) = 60% reduction against a same-level attacker; cloth 0.45x, leather 0.6x, mail 0.8x of plate. Slot shares: chest 35%, head 20%, feet 15%, hands 12%, belt 8%, shield 10%. The percentages a tooltip prints must be computed against the PLAYER level (what you would feel against a same-level monster). Block: chance is whole PERCENT (24 = 24%), amount is FLAT damage removed from a blocked hit. Tiers: plain (drops 1-20, Act 1 Normal), fine (21-40, Act 2 / Veteran), masterwork (41-60, Act 3 / Legend). Tiers are the D2 normal/exceptional/elite ladder: same shapes, bigger numbers. levelReq: the character level needed = max(base.levelReq, ceil(0.8 * ilvlMin of the item's highest affix tier)) — see affixes.json. req: minimum ATTRIBUTES (str/agi/int/spi). proficiency: the armour weight or weapon class the character's Path must allow (`proficiency` table below). dropLevel: the lowest ITEM LEVEL at which this base can be rolled (rarity.json `basePick` says how a base is chosen). Units: every `pct` value is whole percentage points (4 = +4%). Code converts with /100 in ONE place. Never store fractions. grid: w x h cells in the 10x4 bag (ruling 11). hand: HOW it is held, the one field every reader asks (js/rules/hands.js) and the first line of the item card: 'one' = One-handed (main hand, or the off hand for a dual-wielder), 'two' = Two-handed (takes both hands; a second one in the off hand only with the Doubled Grasp passive, a Vanguard skill), 'main' = Main hand only (wands, sceptres), 'off' = Off hand only (shields, foci, quivers). hands: 2 = takes the off-hand slot too (kept equal to hand 'two'). offhandOk: kept equal to hand 'one'. Who may dual-wield is the proficiency table's dualWield + dualWieldClasses (Rogue Path; the Weaponmaster spec). pairsWith: a quiver only works with a bow or crossbow in the main hand. look: a hint for the Chibi 2.6 model (avatar-3d gear-catalog kinds first: dagger/sword/axe/mace/bow/crossbow/staff/wand, hood/cap/helm, robe/jerkin/hauberk/cuirass, gloves, shoes/boots, shield/focus/quiver, belt, ring/amulet). Counts: 169 bases, 93 droppable in Act 1 (dropLevel <= 20).

ladders.attributeReq: characters start at 12 in each attribute (+5 a level). weapons: primary attribute 8 + 2.5*L; leather agi 8 + 2L; mail str 8 + 2L; plate str 12 + 2L; cloth int 5 + L

proficiency._doc: Which armour weights and weapon classes each Path (and the two first hybrid specs) may use. Wanderer is level 1-2. A spec ADDS to its Path (plate at the spec pick, ruling 2). Mage stays cloth so cloth never becomes pointless; the Spellblade hybrid gets leather at 10. Healer hybrids (Paladin) get mail then plate at 10.

specAdds._doc: Spec picks at level 10 add these (js/rules/items.js profOf reads specAdds[spec], plus fighter_any for every Fighter spec). Fighter specs are the only way to plate besides the Paladin hybrid.
